QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_109

question.text: A speculator is bullish on TCS. TCS spot is Rs. 3,500 and TCS futures are quoting at Rs. 3,530. He has two choices: buy 1,000 shares in cash (Rs. 35 lakhs) or buy 5 lots of futures (lot size 200, margin 15%). Assume that, by the planned exit, both TCS spot AND TCS futures rise by Rs. 175 per share (a 5% move on spot, with the same Rs. 175 absolute increase on the futures square-off price). Compare the return on investment for both strategies.

answer.text: Cash market: 5% return on Rs. 35 lakhs = Rs. 1,75,000 (5% ROI). Futures: same Rs. 1,75,000 profit but on margin of Rs. 5,29,500 = approximately 33% ROI. Futures deliver higher ROI due to leverage
Both strategies give 5% return because the underlying price change is the same
Cash market gives higher return because there is no cost of carry
Futures give lower return because the entry price (3,530) is higher than spot (3,500)

explanation.text: The Logic: Step-by-step calculation under the stem's assumption that futures and spot both rise by Rs. 175 per share at exit: Cash market: - Investment = 1,000 x 3,500 = Rs. 35,00,000 - Profit = 1,000 x 175 = Rs. 1,75,000 - ROI = 1,75,000 / 35,00,000 = 5% Futures market: - Exposure = 5 lots x 200 x 3,530 = Rs. 35,30,000 - Profit = (1,000 shares) x (Rs. 3,530 + 175 - 3,530) = 1,000 x 175 = Rs. 1,75,000 - Margin = 35,30,000 x 15% = Rs. 5,29,500 - ROI on margin = 1,75,000 / 5,29,500 = approximately 33% The Trap: Option B confuses absolute profit (similar in rupee terms) with ROI on capital deployed - leverage flips the ROI even when the underlying moves identically. Option C ignores leverage entirely. Option D mis-reads the futures entry premium as a permanent disadvantage rather than a starting basis. The audit flagged the original because the stem gave only a 5% spot move and never pinned the futures exit price, so the Rs. 1,75,000 futures profit was an approximation rather than a unique result. Note: The original stem said only "TCS rises 5%" without specifying the futures square-off price. The stem has been tightened to state that both spot and futures rise by Rs. 175 per share at exit. This pins the futures profit at exactly Rs. 1,75,000 and makes the 5% cash ROI vs ~33% futures ROI uniquely correct (NISM Series VIII p.93).
